paragraphs: Start by reviewing the morning harvest block and slope, then warm up the machine and inspect oil and hydraulics. Operate a harvester to cut marked trees into standard logs and pile them during the morning. On steep ground in the afternoon, get out to inspect the terrain before moving and avoid water-conservation zones. Work with the skidder to bring logs roadside and assist with scaling, then grease the equipment and complete maintenance records before finishing.

In short, they operate harvesters to turn trees safely into logs. Work includes running harvesting, piling, and skidding machinery, assessing terrain and routes, performing maintenance, following safety rules and harvesting limits, and assisting with scaling and loading.
